patchedDependenciesComments.immer: this fixes typecheck in mobile app, see https://github.com/reduxjs/redux-toolkit/issues/1806
patchedDependenciesComments.react-native-wagmi-charts@2.10.0: 2.10.0 unconditionally reserves 40px of chart height for x-axis cursor labels, so small inline sparklines (e.g. the 20px chart in mobile token rows) draw into negative height and render cut off/shifted (CONS-2662). Only reserve the space when the chart is taller than the reservation. Should be upstreamed.
patchedDependenciesComments.@shopify/react-native-performance@4.1.2: RN 0.81 compat: Android getExportedCustomDirectEventTypeConstants must return a mutable map; iOS Swift bridging header switched to bracketed framework include. Should be upstreamed to Shopify.
patchedDependenciesComments.react-native-tab-view@3.5.2: Fixes warning on profile screens with spreading key from props. Fixed in react-native-tab-view <4.0.0-alpha.7
patchedDependenciesComments.react-native-sortables@1.10.0: Fabric: favorites grid wedges after a few reorders — a tile stops lifting and reordering freezes. (1) MeasurementsProvider always flushes immediately and never gates on exact measuredItemKeys===itemsCount; removeItemMeasurements reassigns shared values; and item measurements are diffed against itemWidths/itemHeights instead of a JS-side cache of the last onLayout — that cache went stale whenever sizes were dropped from the shared values (item unmount, data change), after which an unchanged re-measure was skipped forever and the key stayed in indexToKey with no size, unliftable and unsortable. (2) calculateLayout uses a fallback cross-size when one item is missing a measurement instead of returning null. (3) useItemZIndex only elevates the active item. (4) LayerProvider updateLayer is a no-op. (5) DragProvider drops upstream's per-item `activationAnimationProgress > 0` activation guard: it rejects long-press on the tile you just dropped, and rejects it permanently whenever that withTiming(0) doesn't land on exactly 0 — the 'one tile stops lifting while the others work' symptom. Replaced by a time-boxed drop-settle window that only *delays* activation; the window must never fail() the gesture, because fail() outside a gesture event breaks that item's native handler for good. Every item's position/animation is also snapped after each drop. (6) ItemsProvider skips React node rebuilds on index-only reorders (prevents remounting item content on every drop). (7) useItemLayoutFabric clears transforms immediately on drop so hit-testing matches the visual slot (esp. odd tile in an incomplete row). App defers Redux persist until Done. Should be upstreamed.

patchedDependenciesComments.@expo/metro-config@54.0.9: Fixes 'TypeError: Invalid URL' on every Fast Refresh in HMR serializer fork (build/serializer/fork/hmrJSBundle.js). Expo's fork calls 'new URL(options.clientUrl)' where clientUrl is a legacy Node url.Url object (from url.parse); Url doesn't override toString, so WHATWG URL coerces it to '[object Object]' and throws. Upstream Metro avoids this by passing url.format(options.clientUrl). Patch round-trips via node:url format() at both call sites (also fixes a sibling .toString() in prepareModule that was silently producing '[object Object]' sourceUrls in dev source maps). Should be upstreamed.
patchedDependenciesComments.zod@4.3.6: Enables jitless mode by default to avoid CSP unsafe-eval violations in browser extension content scripts. See https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/4461
patchedDependenciesComments.@ethersproject/providers@5.7.2: ENS v2 support adapted from @ensdomains/ethers-patch-v5 with tunneling batch gateway
patchedDependenciesComments.webpack@5.90.0: Pinned for Storybook compatibility — webpack 5.105.4 breaks Storybook module bundling. Webpack security CVEs (GHSA-4vvj-4cpr-p986, GHSA-8fgc-7cc6-rx7x, GHSA-38r7-794h-5758) are accepted risk for this dev-only build tool
patchedDependenciesComments.react-native@0.85.3: 1) Makes the hermesc path in hermes-engine.podspec relative to PODS_ROOT so the absolute home-dir path isn't baked into Podfile.lock checksums (per-machine/CI drift). See https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/54891. 2) Skips layout-metrics consumption for yoga children owned by another shadow-tree generation (Reanimated clones share child yoga nodes): consuming them cleared hasNewLayout on the owning tree, leaving views invisible but mounted (ghost bottom sheets) and tripping the dev-only YGNodeGetOwner assert / SIGABRT (INFRA-2390). Drop when https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/52349 is fixed upstream. 3) BaseTextInputShadowNode measures the props text whenever it differs from state.reactTreeAttributedString (the same comparison updateStateIfNeeded uses to push it, and Android's rule); only an unchanged props text lets the empty native state win. Otherwise a paste into a field the user had cleared was laid out at zero width on iOS Fabric (INFRA-4248), while uncontrolled inputs (defaultValue) the user cleared still measure as empty. Guard unchanged upstream since at least RN 0.73 Fabric iOS and still on main as of 2026-09-29; Android already compares props against state and is unaffected. No upstream issue yet; add one here as the drop condition when filed. 4) RCTUITextField names an explicit default NSParagraphStyle in defaultTextAttributes and in the attributed placeholder whenever the attributes omit one: UIKit merges the setter into the field's existing attributes and the placeholder label caches its last paragraph style, so a recycled field kept a previous owner's lineHeight and drew text/placeholder low and clipped in any TextInput without an explicit lineHeight (INFRA-4247). Upstream main (2026-09-29) still has the unpatched RCTUITextField and no issue tracks the recycling case; related: facebook/react-native#37465 (Paper lineHeight alignment) and #53092 (new-arch lineHeight alignment). Drop when upstream RCTUITextField sets an explicit paragraph style, or when an upstream issue we file is fixed.
patchedDependenciesComments.@gorhom/bottom-sheet@5.2.13: Seeds containerHeight from the first measured layout when still INITIAL_LAYOUT_VALUE, fixing zero-height sheets under the new architecture (Fabric).
patchedDependenciesComments.expo-constants@18.0.13: Xcode 26's shallow bundle format doesn't pre-create EXConstants.bundle before the :before_compile script runs; mkdir -p the destination dir to avoid an ENOENT on the JS config write.
patchedDependenciesComments.expo-modules-core@56.0.16: vite 8's rolldown bundler errors with MISSING_EXPORT on value imports of the declare-only classes in src/ts-declarations/global.ts (esbuild silently allowed them); switch them to type-only imports. Should be upstreamed to Expo.
patchedDependenciesComments.react-native-svg@15.12.1: Holds RNSVGImage's RCTImageResponseObserverProxy in a shared_ptr so the Fabric image observer outlives in-flight callbacks (fixes a use-after-free crash on <Image> under Fabric).
patchedDependenciesComments.i18next@23.10.0: Adds $NoUndefinedValues and applies it to the t() options argument so t() rejects possibly-undefined interpolation values at compile time (e.g. t('k', { v: maybeUndefined }) is now a type error). Resource-type-independent — works despite this repo erasing resources to Record<string,string> for typecheck perf, which disables i18next's own placeholder typing.
patchedDependenciesComments.@expo/require-utils@56.1.3: typescript >= 7.0.2 resolves its "." export to a version-only stub with no compiler API, so loadTypescript() would hand Expo config evaluation a ts without transpileModule and crash at ts.ModuleKind (breaks the Android/iOS native builds at expo-constants createExpoConfig). Treat the stub like typescript-not-installed so the module.stripTypeScriptTypes fallback transpiles app.config.ts. Should be upstreamed to Expo; drop when @expo/require-utils supports TS 7 (still unfixed as of 57.0.1).
patchedDependenciesComments.react-native-gesture-handler@3.2.1: Three Android hunks; all three verified still absent as of 3.3.0-nightly-20260828 (3.2.1 is still `latest`), so none of them is fixed by a bump. (1) RNGestureHandlerDetectorView.setModuleId tolerates moduleId changing on a live view: globalThis._RNGH_MODULE_ID advances every time the native module re-inits (JS reload / RN context recreation) and Fabric re-applies the new id to still-mounted detector views, where upstream's `assert(this.moduleId == -1)` crashes with 'Tried to change moduleId of a native detector'. Replaced with a detachAllHandlers() teardown so handlers bound to the previous registry are released first; mirrors iOS updateProps, which reassigns _moduleId freely. REMOVE WHEN: upstream stops asserting write-once in setModuleId. (2) ButtonViewGroup finalizes its managed NativeViewGestureHandler when the app window loses focus. A window opening over the app (native context menu, dialog, permission prompt) keeps the tail of the touch stream, so that handler never reaches a terminal state and every RNGH-button-backed pressable in the app dies until relaunch, while raw Gesture.Tap surfaces keep working. Upstream knows this shape: the ButtonViewGroup.requestDisallowInterceptTouchEvent override (upstream #4367, in 3.2.1) only fires when the call comes from below the button, and the view taking the touch is an ancestor; upstream #4441 (3.3.0) adds a deferred shouldCancelOnNativeTouchGrab sweep for the ScrollView case. Neither covers this: #4441 arms the sweep only between onNativeDispatchStart/End, i.e. inside super.dispatchTouchEvent, and our grab arrives from ContextMenuView.onLongPress — which Android's GestureDetector delivers from a posted Handler message — and on the close path from onWindowFocusChanged, both outside any dispatch pass. REMOVE WHEN: upstream finalizes a button's managed handler on window-focus loss, or otherwise handles a native touch grab raised outside touch dispatch. (3) That same managed handler no longer cancels the JS responder. It backs the button's own press and its view is the responder target, so cancelling on activation — which lands on the first move past the tap timeout — made RN deliver touch-cancel instead of touch-end, silently dropping onPress and any responder-timed onLongPress for every press that moved at all. This is upstream's own rule extended, not a fight with it: upstream #4297 opted the internal root handler out of the same flag for the same reason (restoring stock RN semantics, where core cancels the responder only through explicit onChildStartedNativeGesture calls from ScrollView / SwipeRefreshLayout, plus iOS parity), and the managed button handler landed in 3.2.0 after that PR. Scoped to the button's own handler, so ScrollView and RN core still cancel the responder through their own paths and scroll-vs-press arbitration is unchanged. Not reachable from JS: Touchable/PressableWithTouchable do not expose cancelsTouchesInView. REMOVE WHEN: upstream sets cancelsJSResponder=false on the managed button handler, or exposes it as a prop. All three should be upstreamed.
patchedDependenciesComments.danger@11.2.6: danger's transpiler gates its native-TS path on a bare require.resolve('typescript'), which typescript >= 7.0.2 satisfies with a version-only stub that has no transpileModule — danger would then crash transpiling dangerfile.ts on every PR. Gate on transpileModule actually existing so danger keeps using its babel fallback (same behavior as under 7.0.1-rc, whose missing "." export made the resolve throw). Drop when danger supports TS 7 (still unfixed as of 13.0.10).
patchedDependenciesComments.uniwind@1.7.0: css-processor parseRuleRec overwrites the inherited selector config when it enters a nested pseudo rule: `dark:active:`/`dark:focus:` lower to `&:focus` nested inside `&:where(.dark, .dark *)`, and the nested rule replaced the inherited theme='dark' with null, so the declaration lost its theme gate on native and applied in both themes (INFRA-3264). Merge the nested rule's selector config with the inherited one and restore it after recursion (instead of nulling, which also leaked a cleared config to sibling rules). Same change in all five shipped copies of the processor (src + dist/common + dist/module + both dist/metro transformer bundles — Metro executes the cjs). Should be upstreamed to uni-stack/uniwind. Also: height range media features now resolve to minHeight/maxHeight and are evaluated against screen height instead of being ignored (INFRA-3281). CAUTION on version bumps: bun silently ignores a patchedDependencies entry whose version key does not match the resolved version (no error, no warning), so on any uniwind bump verify the patch still applies (the parity dist-drift gate in packages/tailwind goes red if it did not).
